abstract: Software synthesizers expose dozens of coupled controls, many of them redundant or perceptually inert at typical operating points. This paper presents a two-stage, measure-and-validate framework that ranks parameters by their influence on the audio output and then checks that ranking against an independent, variance-based experiment. Every rendered clip is normalized to -23 LUFS and described by five spectral fingerprints, so that gain shifts cannot masquerade as timbral change. The Sweep Test scores each parameter by spectral deviation over a 101-step sweep; the Sobol Test scores it by summed per-cell variance over a 128-point Sobol excitation. Across five architecturally distinct synthesizers (TorchSynth, Pyo, Pedalboard, Csound, and FluidSynth) spanning 48 to 76 parameters, the two tests agree at Spearman ρ= 0.82-0.96 (p-values \le 7.2 \times 10^{-15}) on the four engines that render deterministically, and at ρ= 0.32 on the one with process-level render noise--a diagnostic of that engine rather than of the method. The strong correlations survive reducing the Sobol budget from 128 to 32 points, and the complete analysis costs a one-time offline budget of about 66,000 renders.

oneSentenceThesis: 把合成器当黑盒，用 101 步单参数扫描打分再用 128 次 Sobol 扰动的输出方差独立验证，在四个确定性引擎上排序高度一致而在有渲染噪声的引擎上失配，结论只在中点工作点和单音触发条件下成立且总代价约 66000 次离线渲染。
